1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Compute the result for a game of Hex / Polygon.
4: 
5: The abstract boardgame known as [Hex][hex] / Polygon / CON-TAC-TIX is quite simple in rules, though complex in practice.
6: Two players place stones on a parallelogram with hexagonal fields.
7: The player to connect his/her stones to the opposite side first wins.
8: The four sides of the parallelogram are divided between the two players (i.e. one player gets assigned a side and the side directly opposite it and the other player gets assigned the two other sides).
9: 
10: Your goal is to build a program that given a simple representation of a board computes the winner (or lack thereof).
11: Note that all games need not be "fair".
12: (For example, players may have mismatched piece counts or the game's board might have a different width and height.)
13: 
14: The boards look like this:
15: 
16: ```text
17: . O . X .
18:  . X X O .
19:   O O O X .
20:    . X O X O
21:     X O O O X
22: ```
23: 
24: "Player `O`" plays from top to bottom, "Player `X`" plays from left to right.
25: In the above example `O` has made a connection from left to right but nobody has won since `O` didn't connect top and bottom.
26: 
27: [hex]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hex_%28board_game%29

This is the classic Hex/Connect problem. The board is a parallelogram made of hexagonal cells, and each row is indented by one space. Player O plays from top to bottom, and player X plays from left to right.

The standard solution: parse the board into a grid. Each row r has r+1 cells (for an n×n board). A cell at (row, col) is adjacent to the following cells:
- (row+1, col) — down-left
- (row+1, col+1) — down-right
- (row-1, col) — up-left
- (row-1, col+1) — up-right
- (row, col+1) — right
- (row, col-1) — left

For player X: a win means connecting the left edge to the right edge. A cell on the left edge is one where col == 0 (the first cell of the row). A cell on the right edge is one where col == row (the last cell of the row).

For player O: a win means connecting the top edge to the bottom edge. Top edge: row == 0. Bottom edge: row == n-1.

Implement it with BFS/DFS from all cells of the player's starting edge, and check whether any cell on the opposite edge is reachable.

Parsing: strip the leading spaces from each line, and split the remainder by spaces. Note that the board string in the tests has leading whitespace due to indentation — strip() each line and skip empty lines.
